nodes.name: Hydrothermal NiFe-LDH Growth
nodes.procedure: The 3D NiFe-LDH NP film was synthesized using nickel and iron nitrates as metal sources and urea as the precipitant under hydrothermal conditions at 120 °C. At this temperature, urea decomposed into ammonia, which created an alkaline environment, and carbonate, which served as the intercalated anion. After hydrothermal reaction, a brown film was coated on the surface of nickel foam.

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show mesoporous NiFe-LDH film with nanoplates grown vertically on Ni substrate, distance between nanoplates ~100 nm, film thickness 200-300 nm, individual nanoplates have crumpled hexagonal morphology with lateral size ~200 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: SEM images of the as-synthesized NiFe-LDH film at different magnifications (Fig. 2B and C) showed that the LDH film was mesoporous with nanoplates grown vertically on the Ni substrate.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals individual NiFe-LDH nanoplates are very thin.
nodes.evidence_snippet: An individual nanoplate from the film had a crumpled and hexagonal morphology, with a lateral size of ~200 nm and was very thin, as revealed by TEM (inset of Fig. 2C).

properties.morphology: network of interconnected pores and walls

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows series of Bragg reflections matching typical LDH materials profile (peaks marked '#' denote Ni substrate).
nodes.evidence_snippet: XRD data showed a series of Bragg reflections, which matched well with the typical profile of LDH materials (the peaks marked ''#'' denote the Ni substrate, Fig. 2D).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms presence of Fe and Ni on film surface; Ni 2p3/2 at 855.7 eV (Ni²⁺) and Fe 2p3/2 at 713.7 eV (Fe³⁺); atomic ratio Ni:Fe ~3:1.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The binding energy peak of Ni 2p3/2 and Fe 2p3/2 is located at 855.7 eV and 713.7 eV (Fig. 2E and F), respectively, indicating the +2 and +3 oxidation states of Ni and Fe. The atomic ratio of Ni and Fe was ~3:1...

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX mapping shows nickel and iron elements homogeneously distributed in the cross-linked 3D architecture.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EDX mapping analysis (Fig. S2, ESI†) showed that both the nickel and iron elements were homogeneously distributed in the cross-linked 3D architecture.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman at 1.2 V shows broad band at 528 cm⁻¹ indicating disordered NiFe-LDH; at 1.6 V (OER condition) shows bands at 476 and 556 cm⁻¹ indicating conversion to NiOOH with structural defects.
nodes.evidence_snippet: At 1.2 V, where OER did not occur, the Raman spectrum of the NiFe-LDH film showed a broad band located at 528 cm⁻¹ (Fig. 5)... At an oxygen evolution potential of 1.6 V, the disappearance of the former band and the appearance of two new bands (at 476 and 556 cm⁻¹) indicated the conversion of the LDH into NiOOH...
